\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منظمة} (munaẓẓama)}{منظمة (munaẓẓama)}]{\ar{منظمة} (munaẓẓama) — an organization}

\label{lesson:AR-C385-munazzama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for agriculture, then the Arabic for development.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منظمة}}
\textbf{\ar{منظمة}} — \emph{munaẓẓama} — \textquotedblleft{}an organization\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تساعد} \ar{المنظمة} \ar{الأطفال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tusāʿidu al-munaẓẓama al-aṭfāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The organization helps children.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منظمة}} (\emph{munaẓẓama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-ẓ-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to string pearls, to put in order\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Munaẓẓama} is a Form II passive participle, feminine, something put in order: an organization.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munaẓẓama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munaẓẓama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tusāʿidu al-munaẓẓama al-aṭfāl.} — The organization helps children.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for agriculture, then the Arabic for development, then say \emph{munaẓẓama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{منظمة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An organization\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جمعية} (jamʿiyya)}{جمعية (jamʿiyya)}]{\ar{جمعية} (jamʿiyya) — an association}

\label{lesson:AR-C385-jamiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for development, then the Arabic for an organization.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جمعية}}
\textbf{\ar{جمعية}} — \emph{jamʿiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}an association\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعمل} \ar{أمي} \ar{في} \ar{جمعية} \ar{للنساء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿmalu ummī fī jamʿiyya li-n-nisāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother works in a women's association.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جمعية}} (\emph{jamʿiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-m-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to gather, to bring together\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Jamʿiyya} is a gathering: an association, a society.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamʿiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamʿiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿmalu ummī fī jamʿiyya li-n-nisāʾ.} — My mother works in a women's association.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for development, then the Arabic for an organization, then say \emph{jamʿiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جمعية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An association\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نقابة} (niqāba)}{نقابة (niqāba)}]{\ar{نقابة} (niqāba) — a trade union}

\label{lesson:AR-C385-niqaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an organization, then the Arabic for an association.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نقابة}}
\textbf{\ar{نقابة}} — \emph{niqāba} — \textquotedblleft{}a trade union\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دافعت} \ar{النقابة} \ar{عن} \ar{العمال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dāfaʿat an-niqāba ʿan al-ʿummāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The union defended the workers.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نقابة}} (\emph{niqāba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-q-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to bore through; a chief\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{naqīb} is the chief of a group; \emph{niqāba} is his office, and now a trade union.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niqāba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niqāba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāfaʿat an-niqāba ʿan al-ʿummāl.} — The union defended the workers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an organization, then the Arabic for an association, then say \emph{niqāba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نقابة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A trade union\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مجلس} (majlis)}{مجلس (majlis)}]{\ar{مجلس} (majlis) — a council}

\label{lesson:AR-C385-majlis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an association, then the Arabic for a trade union.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مجلس}}
\textbf{\ar{مجلس}} — \emph{majlis} — \textquotedblleft{}a council\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اجتمع} \ar{مجلس} \ar{المدينة} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ijtamaʿa majlis al-madīna ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The city council met yesterday.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{مجالس}, \emph{majālis}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مجلس}} (\emph{majlis}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-l-s}, \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Majlis} is a noun of place, a place of sitting: a council.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{majlis}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{majlis}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijtamaʿa majlis al-madīna ams.} — The city council met yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an association, then the Arabic for a trade union, then say \emph{majlis} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مجلس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A council\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عضو} (ʿuḍw)}{عضو (ʿuḍw)}]{\ar{عضو} (ʿuḍw) — a member}

\label{lesson:AR-C385-udw}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a trade union, then the Arabic for a council.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عضو}}
\textbf{\ar{عضو}} — \emph{ʿuḍw} — \textquotedblleft{}a member\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أخي} \ar{عضو} \ar{في} \ar{نادي} \ar{الشطرنج}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhī ʿuḍw fī nādī ash-shaṭranj.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother is a member of the chess club.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أعضاء}, \emph{aʿḍāʾ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عضو}} (\emph{ʿuḍw}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ḍ-w}, \textquotedblleft{}a limb\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{ʿuḍw} is a limb of the body, and so a member of any body of people.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿuḍw}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhī ʿuḍw fī nādī ash-shaṭranj.} — My brother is a member of the chess club.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a trade union, then the Arabic for a council, then say \emph{ʿuḍw} again
\end{itemize}
